audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer spells Kled's Q "Beartrap on a Rope" as one word, in 25 separate strings.
audit.why: Riot's name is "Bear Trap on a Rope" (two words). It is the single most-repeated string in this matchup entry - it appears in tldr, winCon, enemyWin, three phase whys, seven breakdown keys, loading, focus, ahead, dosFull and seven report cards - so the error is on screen almost everywhere a player looks.
audit.corrected: All 25 occurrences respelled "Bear Trap on a Rope".
sources: champ-data/_kits/kled.json (Q names ["Bear Trap on a Rope"])

audit.whatIsWrong: content spikes[1].text writes "Chaaaaaaaaarge!!!" with nine a's.
audit.why: Riot's spelling is "Chaaaaaaaarge!!!" with exactly eight a's. The packet did not flag this one at all - its suspectNames list for Kled is empty - so it would have survived the automated pass.
audit.corrected: Respelled with eight a's inside the rewritten spikes[1].text.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gives Kled 6 of 7 stages while Zac wins 58.21%.
audit.why: Kled genuinely owns levels 1 through 4-5 on mounted trades, but the chart cannot hand the losing side six stages. Level 6 is not his either: Chaaaaaaaarge!!! is 140/125/110, the longest ultimate cooldown in this matchup pool, against Zac's 120/105/90.
audit.corrected: Kled / Kled / Kled / Kled / Skill / Zac / Zac.

audit.whatIsWrong: content mid says to "poke his courage down toward a dismount".
audit.why: That inverts the mechanic. Courage is what Kled BUILDS by fighting in order to remount; you cannot poke it down. What you deplete to dismount him is Skaarl's health bar. A player following this line would trade to reduce a bar that only ever goes up when he trades.
audit.corrected: Rewritten to chip Skaarl's health and deny him the fights that refill courage.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kled.json (P: "Kled can restore Skaarl's courage by fighting enemies. At maximum courage, Kled remounts")

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing anywhere mentions that Jousting is recastable, or what Kled's Q becomes once he is dismounted.
audit.why: Two decisive omissions. First, Jousting can be cast again to dash back through the initial target, so a Kled who dashes in is never committed - the advice to punish him after he engages is only true once the recast window has passed. Second, dismounted his Q is replaced by Pocket Pistol, which knocks Kled himself backwards AND restores courage, so chasing a dismounted Kled both fails and pays for his remount.
audit.corrected: Recast added to whys[2] and mid; Pocket Pistol added to spikes[2].text.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kled.json (E: "Kled can cast this ability again to dash back through his initial target"; Q: "When dismounted, this ability is replaced by Pocket Pistol, a ranged gun blast that knocks back Kled and restores courage")

audit.whatIsWrong: No trade-timing tell for Violent Tendencies.
audit.why: Violent Tendencies is a fixed four-attack window whose fourth attack deals more damage, on 13/12/11/10/9. The window is countable: the punish is to be out of range for the fourth auto, not to disengage when you see the cast.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kled.json (W: "massive attack speed for four attacks. The fourth attack deals more damage")

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither layer notes that Zac's Q and Kled's Q have identical 800 range.
audit.why: Both are 800-range single-target grabs that pull. The lane's opening exchange is therefore a genuine first-cast race at an identical distance rather than a range mismatch, which is what the missing-interactions file means by "whoever lands it first owns the trade".

notes: The packet lists no suspectNames for Kled, yet this entry carries two real ability-name errors: "Beartrap on a Rope" (one word) in 25 full-layer strings, and "Chaaaaaaaaarge!!!" with nine a's in content spikes[1].text. The near-miss detector missed both, so the same class of error is likely sitting in other matchups it also reported clean. The two win[] edits are short label fields and will not survive a literal +/-10% length band.
